RPL10.gate_coupling_note: Back gate is more weakly coupled than top gate because the bottom hBN is thicker. Diagonal features in gate space can look skewed relative to n/D coordinates.
RPL10.nd_transform_note: Use gate-space coordinates for output, but remember that humans often reinterpret these maps in carrier density n and displacement field D. Approximate n scales with Vbg/dbg + Vtg/dtg and D scales with Vtg/dtg - Vbg/dbg.

RPL19.gate_coupling_note: RPL19 has a thinner top dielectric than bottom dielectric, so top-gate motion changes the state more strongly than an equal back-gate step.
RPL19.nd_transform_note: Use gate-space coordinates for output, but treat diagonal slopes as gate-space projections of simpler structure in n/D. Approximate n scales with Vbg/dbg + Vtg/dtg and D scales with Vtg/dtg - Vbg/dbg.
